messages.text: Take {gift_item}. I may not have a trade, but I know how to say thanks.
Here, {gift_item}. Maybe one of us will find the perfect use for it.
Good, {gift_item} worked. See? I can be useful without a workstation.
{tested_villager} liked it? Excellent. I am putting that under possible talents.
Ah. Then my career in advice pauses here. Try {alternative_gift} for {gift_subject}.
{gift_item} was wrong? Let us call it research. {alternative_gift} should work better.
This is why nobody pays me for advice. Try {alternative_gift}.
You came back? Fair. My next guess is {alternative_gift}.

openings.text: Mind the job site I have not found yet. What do you need?

closings.text: Back to looking useful before anyone notices, then.

lines.text: Finding the right work is harder when everyone asks if you found it yet.
Work is work. Finding the right work is the tricky part.
A fair chance can look a lot like standing around until the right bell rings.
If you see a spare job site, do mention it kindly.
Waiting for work is still work if you look worried enough.
Where do I fit? Somewhere useful, I hope, preferably before supper.
I once followed the bell hoping it meant opportunity. It meant hurry.
Unemployed jokes are flexible. That is what I keep telling myself.
That was idle talk, and I would know.
People with trades get tasks. People without trades get errands.
A fair chance is easier to ask for than to recognize.
I organized a barrel once. For a moment, everyone thought I had a calling.
I am trying to look useful, not involved.

pacify.text: Fine. I have enough problems without carrying this one too.
Even without a trade, I know that should be {emerald_cost} {emeralds}.
No. I may not have work, but I still have sense.
